intent: Accumulates wall-clock time spent in named sub-phases of a repeating operation and periodically logs a percentage breakdown of where the time went.

objects.name: SPerformanceTimer
objects.role: tracks start/stop intervals per named type, sums durations into totals, logs a breakdown every 10s

intent: RAII-scoped timer (AutoTimerTime) built on AutoTimer, which accumulates time spent in bracketed sections and logs the percentage of wall-clock time spent inside them every 10 seconds.

objects.name: AutoTimer
objects.role: owns running total and 10s logging interval; start()/stop() bracket a timed section

objects.name: AutoTimerTime
objects.role: RAII guard calling AutoTimer::start on construction and AutoTimer::stop on destruction

misfits.why: the header's own comment notes a second, unrelated class also named AutoTimer exists in BedrockCore.h (a per-command timing guard) - same name, different purpose, genuinely confusable

name_fit.note: describes its function, but collides with BedrockCore::AutoTimer, an unrelated class of the same name

naming_quality.note: the name clash with BedrockCore::AutoTimer is the main issue; otherwise consistent convention

intent: Variadic function template that launches a thread like std::thread but captures any exception the callable throws and delivers it back to the caller through a std::future.

objects.name: SThread
objects.role: wraps f(args...) in try/catch on a new thread, routes return value or caught exception through a promise/future, returns {thread, future}

name_fit.note: PascalCase, S-prefixed free function reads as a type/constructor call rather than a function, given repo convention reserves that style for classes

naming_quality.note: S-prefix on a lower-case-callable function template is inconsistent with the repo's S-prefix-for-types convention

intent: Static-only wrapper around a shared mt19937_64 generator providing the repo's common random-number needs: raw 64-bit values, bounded ranges, random alphanumeric strings, and weighted booleans.

objects.name: SRandom
objects.role: all-static utility; rand64/limitedRand64 draw integers, randStr builds an alphanumeric string, randBool does a Bernoulli trial

intent: Keys a separate SSocketPool per hostname so callers can get/return sockets to any number of hosts through one object instead of managing one SSocketPool per host themselves.

objects.name: SMultiHostSocketPool
objects.role: mutex-guarded map<host, SSocketPool>; getSocket/returnSocket find-or-create the per-host pool and delegate to it

location_fit.note: sits naturally next to SSocketPool, which it wraps

intent: RAII guard that installs an on-prepare callback on a SQLite object for the guard's lifetime and removes it on scope exit.

objects.name: AutoScopeOnPrepare
objects.role: holds a reference to the SQLite db and handler pointer; constructor installs/enables the handler, destructor clears it

misfits.why: a libstuff file whose sole purpose is scoping a sqlitecluster/SQLite feature (setOnPrepareHandler/enablePrepareNotifications), and it #includes sqlitecluster/SQLite.h directly - libstuff is meant to be generic and dependency-light, this is SQLite-specific

location_fit.note: depends directly on sqlitecluster/SQLite.h; belongs closer to SQLite than in generic libstuff

naming_quality.note: handler parameter and member both shadow the name _db distinct from the constructor's db/member _db
